title: Context-aware sidebar proposal (WIP)
body:
Context / goal:
The console navigation needs to scale across three axes: breadth (more product surfaces coming), depth (admin and tenant-level pages), and context-sensitivity (users doing task-driven flows should see fewer distractions). This doc captures a pragmatic, iterated proposal for a context-aware left sidebar and routing scaffolding that prioritizes task completion and discoverability while keeping accessibility and performance constraints in mind.

High-level design goals:
- Task-first: reduce cognitive load for primary tasks (deploy model, create route, inspect trace). Show contextual shortcuts and hide unrelated entries.
- Predictable URLs & shallow routing: keep routes bookmarkable and reflect resource hierarchy (project > model > route > run).
- Low visual noise: support three sidebar states (collapsed, focused, full) and clear affordances for switching.
- Gradual progressive disclosure: advanced settings and subpages live in secondary panels or nested lists, not primary nav.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation, ARIA landmarks, and focus management when panels open.
- Performance: sidebar state change should not rehydrate whole app; prefer CSS-driven transforms and minimal React tree changes.

Proposed IA (conceptual):
Top-level hubs (left rail primary items):
- Home (dashboard)
- Projects (project selector + list)
- Models (catalog + pinned models)
- Deployments (routes & pools)
- Observability (traces, logs, metrics)
- Optimize (recommendations, batching)
- Settings (org & billing)

Contextual augmentations (task-driven panels):
- When inside a Project: left rail replaces Home with Project hub (routes, models, users specific to that project).
- When inside a Model: quick actions appear inline (deploy, eval, pin) and the deployments hub highlights related routes.
- When editing a Route: show a condensed route-toolbar in the rail with quick toggles (canary, fallback, rollout percentage).

Sidebar states and behavior:
- Collapsed: icons only, short tooltips, keyboard shortcut to expand. Minimum width to show 6 icons. Persist per-user.
- Focused (task mode): automatically transition when user enters deep flow (e.g., creating route). Shows 2–3 contextual sections with labels and primary CTA. Auto-collapse after idle; user override persists.
- Full: expanded with labels and secondary nav visible. Search input pinned to top of the rail in this state.
Transitions: animate width and fade; avoid reordering items during animation.

Routing patterns and URL taxonomy:
- Keep canonical routes: /projects/:pid/models/:mid, /projects/:pid/deployments/:rid, /org/settings/billing.
- Use query params for ephemeral modes: /projects/:pid/models/:mid?edit=true (editor modal), /deployments?filter=offline.
- Avoid deep nested fragments for state where possible; prefer modal/panel over route for transient steps (e.g., model-upload, token-creation).
- Canonical bookmarkable routes should always land the user in a stable UI state (no ephemeral focused mode unless explicit param present).

Wireframe notes (desktop & tablet):
- Desktop: 3-column layout (left rail, main content, right contextual inspector). Left rail vertical rhythm 16px. Icons 20px. Use divider and micro-separators for hubs.
- Tablet: allow collapse of inspector; rail may auto-collapse to icons after width threshold.
- Mobile: bottom nav with 4 primary hubs (Home, Projects, Deployments, Observability). Project-level navigation surfaces via top breadcrumb + hamburger.

Accessibility specifics:
- Nav should be a single nav landmark with aria-label="Main" and aria-expanded on individual groups.
- Keyboard: home/end to jump, Ctrl/Cmd+K opens quick switcher, arrow keys to traverse collapsed icons.
- Focus trap for modals/panels; when opening contextual inspector, move focus to first actionable item; return focus on close.
- Contrast: ensure 4.5:1 for labels, 3:1 acceptable for disabled states.

Backlog grooming (rough prioritized items):
1) Implement collapsed/full rail states + persistence (P0) — infra: localStorage or user-preference API. Linked ticket: INF-4123.
2) Contextual project hub prototype (P0) — wireframe + Figma + small A/B in staging.
3) Keyboard nav & quick switcher (P1) — depends on accessibility baseline.
4) Route-toolbar micro-interactions (P1) — quick toggles + confirmation to avoid accidental toggles.
5) Mobile bottom-nav spec (P2) — separate shipping milestone.
6) Lazy-load right inspector content (P2) — performance optimization.
7) Analytics tracking points (P1) — nav clicks, mode transitions, quick action usage.

Implementation notes & technical constraints:
- React route-aware components should subscribe only to route slices they need; avoid full-page re-renders when expanding rail.
- Prefer CSS grid + transform for animations; avoid layout thrash.
- Server-side rendering: ensure initial rail state derived from user preference endpoint to avoid flicker.
- Metrics: fire events for state changes and navigation to measure discoverability drop-off.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we allow per-org defaults for rail state vs per-user? (Maya: org default helpful for SRE teams)
- How aggressive should auto-focus mode be? (current idea: only for known long flows — create route, import model)
- Can the contextual inspector be reused across product hubs or will each hub require a bespoke implementation?
- Are there privacy concerns showing pinned model names in collapsed rail tooltips for shared screens?

Notes-to-self / broken thoughts (keep here as we iterate):
- Quick switcher should show recently used resources first (project/model/route). Consider TTL for recency.
- Might be useful to surface rollout status badges directly in rail (tiny red/yellow/green dot) for critical routes. Need performance check.
- Explore keyboard mapping for toggling rail states — don't collide with OS-level mappings (Windows: Win+ used heavily).

Next steps / owners:
- Design: Maya to produce compact and focused wireframes (due 2026-02-02).
- Eng: Ethan to spike persistence and minimal-collapse animation (due 2026-02-12).
- PM: Jordan to draft A/B plan and measurement framework (due 2026-02-20).
- Sync: weekly sync on Fridays 10am PT; add to #console-navigation Slack channel.

Appendix: quick links to artifacts
- Figma file: figma.com/file/Redwood-Console/Sidebar-v2 (work-in-progress frames: "compact", "focused")
- Confluence: Console-IA-2026 (detailed legacy mappings and prior decisions)
- Jira: INF-4123 (rail collapse implementation), INF-4187 (route-toolbar toggles)

If you want a pared-down one-pager for exec: I can extract the TL;DR and P0 asks. This doc will be used as the working spec for the next two sprints; expect changes as design/eng spike findings come in.

-- Jordan
